description: Doubly-ended heap (min-max heap) for Go: O(1) min/max peek, O(log n) Push, Pop, PopMax, Remove, Fix. Generic and heap.Interface APIs, no dependencies.
rules: Import path is github.com/aalpar/deheap; the module has no dependencies outside the Go standard library.
For cmp.Ordered element types, use the generic API: deheap.New[T](), deheap.From(items...), then methods on *Deheap[T].

For custom element types, implement container/heap's heap.Interface and call the package-level functions (deheap.Init, Push, Pop, PopMax, Remove, Fix). Do not call container/heap functions on the same value; they maintain a different invariant.
Call deheap.Init(h) once on a heap.Interface value built from unordered data before any other deheap function.
Pop and PopMax on an empty heap return nil (interface API) or the zero value of T (generic API); check Len() first when the zero value is a valid element.
Peek and PeekMax panic on an empty heap; guard with Len() > 0.
For a fixed-capacity heap, use NewBounded or FromBounded and insert with Offer, which evicts the largest element when full. Push ignores MaxLen.
Use PushPop / PushPopMax instead of Push followed by Pop / PopMax; they are cheaper (no slice growth in the generic API, no bubble-up when the pushed element is already the extremum).
DrainAsc and DrainDesc return iter.Seq[T] and consume the heap; breaking out early leaves the remaining elements in a valid heap.
After mutating an element in place, call Fix with its index; Remove and Fix take a slice index, not a value.
